purpose: Twelfth expanded public source layer focused on hypervalent iodine and iodonium route handles, asymmetric organocatalytic stereocontrol, photoenzymatic and photobiocatalytic cascades, artificial metalloenzyme design, PFAS persistence/degradation critique, RNA/riboswitch ligand route policy, protein-protein interaction mimetics, and solid-supported or encoded-library linker boundaries.

promotion_requirements: explicit precursor structures before template or proposal promotion
separate organoiodine, organocatalytic, photobiocatalytic, artificial-enzyme, PFAS, RNA-targeting, PPI-mimetic, or solid-supported library policy

route-specific reagent class, aryl-transfer handle, catalyst-controlled stereochemistry, excitation/enzyme mode, metalloenzyme scaffold, environmental persistence, RNA binding pocket, PPI epitope, resin linker, tag, and support-cleavage review
oxidant, catalyst, photochemical, biocatalysis, environmental, RNA biological-mode, PPI biological-mode, library provenance, or process-safety review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid quantities, operational procedures, and synthesis conditions
organoiodine, radical/photoenzymatic, PFAS, RNA-probe, PPI, and encoded-library entries are high-level route priors only

families.name: Hypervalent iodine, iodonium, and organoiodine route handles
families.strategic_principle: Separate iodine reagent class, aryl-transfer partner, oxidative role, and leaving-group identity from ordinary arylation or oxidation templates.

families.name: Asymmetric organocatalysis, iminium/enamine activation, and phase-transfer stereocontrol
families.strategic_principle: Expose catalyst activation mode and stereocontrol element as route metadata. Catalyst identity can define the disconnection when product stereochemistry depends on it.

families.name: Photoenzymatic, radical-enzyme, and light-driven biocatalytic cascades
families.strategic_principle: Separate photochemical excitation, enzyme selectivity, radical activation mode, and cascade order. Light and enzyme logic must be tracked together.

families.name: Artificial metalloenzymes, engineered enzymes, and biocatalyst-design route anchors
families.strategic_principle: Separate target transformation from metal cofactor, protein scaffold, substrate scope, and engineering lineage. Catalyst identity is a proposal gate.

families.name: PFAS-like motifs, perfluoroalkyl persistence, degradation, and replacement critique
families.strategic_principle: Separate fluorinated performance motif from persistence, degradation products, and replacement policy. Environmental fate can dominate route critique.

families.name: RNA-targeted ligands, riboswitch binders, and validation-gated RNA probe motifs
families.strategic_principle: Separate parent ligand, RNA structural pocket, validation tag or probe handle, and biological target class. RNA-targeted entries require assay validation before promotion.

families.name: Protein-protein interaction hotspot mimetics, helix mimetics, and constrained epitope ligands
families.strategic_principle: Separate binding epitope, hotspot topology, conformational constraint, and ligand growth vector. PPI topology defines route critique.

families.name: Solid-supported synthesis, resin linkers, encoded-library tags, and parallel-synthesis boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate solution target synthesis from resin linker, support cleavage, tag identity, and library provenance. Support and tag metadata are route-defining.

anchors.name: Organoiodine route handle with reviewed iodine valence, aryl-transfer partner, and oxidative role
Organocatalytic route with reviewed activation mode, catalyst class, and stereochemical outcome
Photoenzymatic cascade with reviewed excitation mode, enzyme selectivity, and radical pathway
Artificial or engineered enzyme with reviewed metal cofactor, scaffold, and substrate scope
PFAS-like fluorinated motif with reviewed persistence, degradation, and replacement policy
RNA-targeted ligand or riboswitch binder with reviewed RNA pocket and validation mode
PPI hotspot mimetic with reviewed epitope topology, constraint, and binding vector
Solid-supported or encoded-library route with reviewed linker, support, cleavage, and tag provenance

disconnections.name: Hypervalent iodine-mediated transformation to substrate plus iodine oxidant or transfer-handle policy

forward_logic: separate substrate synthesis from iodine-mediated oxidative or atom-transfer event
track iodine valence and reagent class as route metadata
flag iodine oxidant entries for safety and scope review
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that make the iodine reagent role explicit instead of treating it as a generic oxidation condition.

evidence.citation: Hypervalent iodine(III) oxidative methodology review provides public context for iodine-mediated route handles.
Iodine(V)-based oxidant review discusses oxidation reactions mediated by high-valent iodine reagents.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit iodine valence, reagent class, and oxidative role

disconnections.name: Iodonium or benziodoxole product logic to aryl/atom-transfer partner plus leaving-group policy

forward_logic: separate aryl donor identity from substrate arylation site
track dummy aryl, atom-transfer, or benziodoxole logic before route scoring
avoid generic arylation disconnections when iodonium selectivity defines feasibility
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use organoiodine transfer entries when donor identity and transfer selectivity are route-defining.

evidence.citation: Diaryliodonium salt review covers arylating-agent context for carbonyl alpha-arylation.

source_notes.summary: The v13 expansion promotes backlog families for organoiodine route handles, asymmetric organocatalysis, photoenzymatic cascades, artificial metalloenzymes, PFAS persistence/degradation critique, RNA/riboswitch ligand strategy, PPI hotspot mimetics, and solid-supported or encoded-library linker boundaries.

Organoiodine, organocatalytic, photobiocatalytic, artificial-enzyme, PFAS, RNA-targeting, PPI-mimetic, and encoded-library records are advisory. Promotion to proposal generation requires explicit chemical, biological, environmental, validation, or library-provenance review as applicable.
